How I Work

My Design Process

Select any stage to explore the approach.

01
Discover
Deep dives into user needs, business goals, and domain context. Stakeholder interviews, heuristic reviews, analytics audits, and competitive analysis — building shared understanding before a single pixel is placed.
02
Define
Synthesising research into clear problem statements, personas, and jobs-to-be-done. Alignment workshops that turn ambiguity into a north star the whole team can design towards — measurable success metrics included.
03
Design
From rapid sketching and information architecture through high-fidelity prototypes and design-system-aligned components. Every decision tied to a user need or measurable outcome — nothing decorative.
04
Validate
Usability testing, A/B experiments, and accessibility audits before final hand-off. Findings translated into concrete design changes — not slide decks. Validation is design, not gatekeeping.
05
Scale
Post-launch monitoring, iteration sprints, and design system contributions that make the next product cheaper and faster to build well. Good design compounds — I plan for that from day one.

Overview & Problem
01
Why an AI ChatBot?

Customer support teams were overwhelmed — 80% of incoming queries were repetitive, yet required a full agent response cycle. Wait times exceeded 8 minutes, customer satisfaction was dropping, and support costs were scaling unsustainably.

!
8+ min average wait time for tier-1 support — users abandoned before receiving help
!
80% of queries were repeat questions — FAQs, status checks, account resets — solvable without a human agent
!
No 24/7 coverage — queries outside business hours went unanswered until the next day, frustrating users
!
Escalations to live agents lacked context — agents had to ask users to repeat everything, creating double friction
~
Existing chatbot was rule-based with rigid menus — users often hit dead ends with no recovery path

"How might we resolve the majority of support queries instantly, while ensuring users who need a human are handed off with full context and no friction?"

🔬
Research & Insights
02
What We Learned From Users
1,200+
Support Tickets
18
User Interviews
5
Intent Clusters
→
Analysed for query clustering and theme extraction — 5 intent clusters covering 83% of all incoming support volume
→
Users don't mind talking to a bot — as long as it solves their problem quickly and doesn't pretend to be human
→
The biggest frustration: being stuck in a loop — when the bot can't understand and offers no exit path
→
Users want the bot to remember context — if they escalate to a human, they should not have to repeat themselves
→
Quick replies and suggested actions tested significantly better than free-text input alone — reduced cognitive load
👤
Persona
03
Meet Arjun — The Frustrated Customer

Arjun Mehta — Digital-native professional · 28 · Mumbai · Impatient, high expectations for digital products

Scenario: Arjun's payment failed but was deducted from his account. He needs a resolution in minutes — he's tried the FAQ and couldn't find help. He opens the chatbot expecting it to either fix the issue or immediately connect him with someone who can. Any friction or dead end will push him to leave a negative review.

Goals
Resolve issue in under 3 minutes · Get a clear answer, not a runaround · Confirmation of resolution immediately · Not repeat himself to multiple agents
Pain Points
Bot doesn't understand his specific issue · Stuck in a loop — same question repeated · No way to reach a human fast · Has to re-explain when escalated
🔄

Conversation Flow Design
05
Core Conversation Architecture

Every flow was designed with three exit states: resolved by bot, handed to human agent with full context, or proactively scheduled callback. No dead ends were allowed.

👋 Greeting + Quick intents
→
🎯 Intent Recognition
→
🤖 Bot-Resolvable / 🚨 Escalation
→
✅ Resolve + Confirm
Escalation Flow — Context-Rich Handoff
→
Bot collects: user ID, issue category, conversation summary, attempted resolutions, and emotional signal (detected from language patterns)
→
Agent receives a pre-populated context card before the conversation begins — user never needs to repeat themselves
→
If no live agent is available, bot offers scheduled callback or async chat — not a dead end
→
Error recovery built into every node — if NLP confidence is below threshold, bot surfaces clarifying questions or a manual category picker
💡
UX Principles Applied
06
Design Decisions That Made the Difference
Bot Personality
Named, warm, efficient. Never pretends to be human. Uses first-person but acknowledges being an AI. Informal tone — approachable without being annoying.
Progressive Disclosure
Start with quick reply chips for common intents — show free-text input only when needed. Reduces cognitive load for 72% of users.
No Dead Ends
Every node has at least one fallback — clarifying question, category picker, or human escalation. "I didn't get that" always includes a recovery path.
Context Persistence
Conversation context maintained across the entire session. When escalated, full transcript and intent summary is passed to the agent automatically.
Time Expectation Setting
Bot always tells users how long an action will take — "I'm checking your account, this takes about 5 seconds" — reduces abandonment.
Micro-copy matters
Every bot message was copyedited for tone, clarity, and empathy. "Done! I've submitted your request — you'll hear back within 2 hours" vs generic confirmations.
📊

07
Measuring Conversational UX Success

Beyond standard UX metrics, conversational AI requires its own measurement framework — tracking not just usability but intent resolution accuracy, escalation quality, and conversation health.

Overview
01
Overview

The goal of this project was to develop a comprehensive design system for M2P to ensure consistency, efficiency, and scalability in UI/UX design across all digital products. This design system would include elements such as typography, color schemes, icons, components, and themes.

BaselineAssetsBuildingAdoptionDesign at scaleGovernanceSatisfaction of usersDesign and code
⚠️
Problem Statement
02
Inconsistent design across projects leads to inefficiencies, fragmented experiences, and scalability challenges.

The product struggles with maintaining design consistency across multiple projects, resulting in inefficiencies, fragmented user experiences, and deviations from brand guidelines.

This lack of standardization increases design debt, slows down development, and creates challenges in scalability and collaboration.

🔬
Research and Analysis
03
M2P Products
Interviews
Conducted interviews with designers, developers, and project managers to understand their pain points and requirements for the design system.
Competitive Analysis
Analyzed existing design systems from leading companies to identify best practices and gather inspiration.
Surveys
Distributed surveys to gather feedback on current design processes and tools.
🗺️
Roadmap - Design System
04
Roadmap - Design System

The roadmap outlines the phased development and implementation plan of the design system, prioritizing core assets and documentation first, followed by iterative enhancements based on user feedback and evolving project needs.

This strategic approach ensures continuous improvement and alignment with organizational goals and user requirements.

⚙️
Principles
05
Design System

A set of standards to manage design at scale by reducing redundancy while creating a shared language and visual consistency across all products.

Based on the research findings, we defined the core requirements for the design system.

📊
Research findings
06
Research findings
→
Create a set of standards to manage design at a scale.
→
Enable consistent 'look and feel' across all M2P digital products.
→
Empower designers to focus on the more complex and actual problems and solutions.
→
Reduce redundancy, and Increase efficiency.
→
Speed up design, handing over, and development — grow fast.
🎨
Design System
07
Colors

A comprehensive set of colors built to support theming, data visualization, and Seamless UI components.

Brand Value
To facilitate recall and establish our brand in the minds of users and customers.
Accessible
The color system provides sufficient contrast ratio and adheres to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines where possible.
Consistent
The color system enables a consistent appearance across varied products and platforms.
Typography
Chose primary and secondary typefaces that align with the agency's brand identity. Defined font sizes, weights, and styles for various text elements (e.g., headings, body text, captions).
🧩
Design System
08
Icons

Curated a set of icons that align with the agency's visual style. Ensured icons are scalable and readable at various sizes.

Components

Identified common UI components needed across projects (e.g., buttons, forms, navigation bars). Designed components to be reusable and adaptable to different contexts.

⚛️
Design System
09
Atomic Design System

The basic design elements of Atomic Design, first coined by Brad Frost, primarily consist of 3 elements: Atoms, Molecules, and Organisms. When stitched together, the design elements ensure consistency and allow unlimited scalability for the Design System.

Core Assets

Core assets in a design system encompass essential elements like typography, color schemes, icons, and reusable components, which ensure consistent branding and design across all digital products.

These foundational assets streamline the design process, fostering uniformity and efficiency in creating cohesive user experiences.

About
01
LuLu Money

LuLu Money is a remittance app that makes cross-border money transfer. It is powered by LuLu Exchange, one of the world's leading financial services company with more than 200 branches worldwide.

With LuLu Money you can transfer money to over 170 countries easily and securely.

Send Money where you wantKnow the current exchange ratesKeep track of your transaction& Many more features...
⚠️
Validating The Problem
02
Validating The Problem

Over the years, although Lulu Money has built strong network in Middle East, South East countries and become famous for cross-border money transfer services, the company now faces the risk of losing the ground in digital business because of:

→
Outdated user experience.
→
Not intuitive enough for new users, sign up is lengthy, not flexible enough to accommodate more products and service, navigation is limited, not engaging enough.
→
Fast-growing competition. People prefer faster, easier and more convenient alternatives.

The current Lulu Exchange Hybrid app was developed in 2018. There was only one product in scope. There is also a plethora of new products that needs to be introduced in the app. The image of the app must also change from a simple remittance app to a digital banking app which provides users a one stop shop for all their payment and personal finance needs.

🎯
The Goal
03
The Goal

To offer competitive mobile money transfer product in both Middle East & South East markets, as a pillar of building a digital bank, by designing the app from scratch to allow users to: Money Transfer, Forex Booking, Bill Payments, Wallets, Mobile Wallet Transfers.

→
It needs to provide improved and intuitive UX along with modern and thoughtful UI.
→
It needs to leverage the advantage of massive agent locations for bridging the gap between online payment and offline cash pickup.
🔄

Key insights from stakeholder sessions:

→
"It's not customer centric, Only Account transfer, no western money like services. There's demand of more products."
→
Migrant workers (Including Blue & White Collar) are sending home money on a regular basis to support their families, education and investments.
→
Blue collar workers are Android users & have limited technical proficiency. Most common apps used: WhatsApp, Facebook, YouTube.
→
Main competitors: Al Mulla (90% transaction confirmed within 5 mins), Western Union.
⭐
User Feedback
06
Collecting user feedback from App & Play Store

We collected almost 321 positive/negative feedback from app & play stores.

Target Customers
The lapsed: Customers who perceive Lulu Money as old-fashioned, and have embraced digital alternatives like Liv, Western Union.

The current: Both loyal and passively involved customers.

The future: People who recognize the brand and would consider Lulu Money when the time comes.
Key Competitive Insight
Fighting for the best fees and exchange rates is too common. Senders often seek the optimal choices of time and convenience, not just cost. First successful transfer matters when acquiring returning users.
🔧
Problem & Solution Valuation
07
Problem Solution
Only Account transfer, no western money like services. Demand of more products.
→
Introducing more features like Cash payout, Mobile wallet, Bill payments etc.
Transaction status is missing.
→
Transaction status feature (Track Transaction) can be introduced for non-login users. For login users, they can go inside activity & see the status.
Multilingual Required.
→
Multilingual feature can be introduced while onboarding or from settings.
Manage Beneficiaries is missing.
→
An option can be brought in navigation bar to add/manage beneficiaries.
Tutorial is missing — Onboarding state is required.
→
While onboarding a new user, a tutorial can be introduced.

QuikGift

QuikGift is a corporate rewards platform specifically designed to streamline and simplify the process of sending and receiving rewards among colleagues within an organization.

About QuikGift
01
QuikGift

QuikGift is a corporate rewards platform specifically designed to streamline and simplify the process of sending and receiving rewards among colleagues within an organization. It enhances employee engagement by fostering a culture of recognition and appreciation, making it easy for team members to acknowledge each other's contributions in real-time.

Integrated seamlessly with Microsoft Teams, QuikGift allows users to send rewards directly within their everyday communication tools, ensuring a smooth and intuitive experience that aligns with existing workflows. This integration empowers companies to boost morale and encourage collaboration through a user-friendly and efficient reward system.

⚠️
Problem Statement
02
Problem Statement

In many organizations, recognizing and rewarding employee contributions is often a delayed or cumbersome process, leading to a lack of real-time appreciation and decreased employee engagement. Existing reward systems are typically fragmented, requiring employees to navigate multiple platforms outside of their daily workflow, which results in low participation and engagement.

Employees and managers struggle to integrate recognition and rewards into their everyday work environment, especially in remote or hybrid settings, where organic recognition is less frequent. This leads to a decline in motivation, productivity, and team morale, as well as difficulty in maintaining a culture of appreciation.

🔄
Design Process for Experience
03
Design Process for Experience

The User-Centered Design (UCD) method is ideal for QuikGift because it places the needs, behaviors, and pain points of users at the forefront of the design process. By involving users at every stage, from research to testing, UCD ensures the product is intuitive, efficient, and aligned with real-world workflows.

Understanding Business Goals
04
Understanding Business Goals

To better understand the business needs of QuikGift, we engaged with multiple stakeholders and identified the following key goals:

→
Workplace Engagement Catalyst: A platform that fosters a culture of appreciation, empowering colleagues to seamlessly recognize and reward each other, enhancing overall employee engagement.
→
Integrated Recognition Hub: A fully embedded solution within Microsoft Teams that simplifies the process of rewarding peers, offering a frictionless experience without leaving their daily workflow.
→
Holistic Rewards Ecosystem: A comprehensive platform that not only facilitates peer-to-peer recognition but also provides insightful analytics and reporting for HR and management.
→
Recognition Experience Expert: A product that deeply understands workplace dynamics, offering tailored reward options and personalized features to ensure meaningful recognition.
⚡
Business Challenges
05
Business Challenges
→
Cultural Alignment: The existing workplace culture may not prioritize recognition, making it difficult to shift attitudes and behaviors towards more frequent peer-to-peer appreciation.
→
Compliance and Security: Addressing data privacy and compliance issues related to employee information and rewards distribution will be critical to maintaining trust and adhering to regulations.
→
Technical Complexity: Establishing a secure and reliable payment processing system requires significant technical expertise — compatibility with existing software infrastructure, handling various payment methods, and integrating with banking systems.
👥
User Groups
06
User Groups
Employees / End Users
Primary users who send and receive rewards. They benefit from the platform's features for recognizing colleagues and can customize their reward choices.
Managers / Leaders
Responsible for recognizing team members' contributions. They utilize the platform to send rewards, track team engagement, and foster a positive work environment.
HR Managers
Oversee employee engagement initiatives and analyze data on recognition patterns. They use the app to manage the overall rewards program and ensure alignment with organizational goals.

User Personas
Jenita Mary · Age 28 · Manager · Chennai
Jenita has been with her company for five years and manages a team of ten. She values team collaboration and seeks to foster a positive work environment where her team feels appreciated and motivated.

Goals: To recognize team members' achievements regularly · To improve team morale and cohesion · To track the effectiveness of recognition efforts.

Enterprise Dashboard · Data Visualisation
📊 Case Study · Enterprise Dashboard · Data Visualisation
Integrated
Dashboard

B2B Enterprise Product · Web · Desktop First · End-to-End UX · Visual Design

Overview
01
Integrated Products Dashboard

A unified enterprise analytics dashboard designed to bring together data from multiple product lines into a single, scannable, and actionable interface for business operators and decision-makers.

⚠️
Problem Statement
02
What Problem Are We Solving?
!
Business operators across product teams had no single view of cross-product performance — data lived in silos across 4+ separate tools
!
Decision-makers had to manually compile reports from multiple sources — time-consuming, error-prone, and always out of date
!
Teams were missing real-time alerts on critical KPI drops — issues were caught too late, impacting revenue and SLA compliance
!
No unified workflow management — approvals, escalations, and action items handled through email and chat, with no visibility into status

"How might we give operators a single source of truth — real-time, actionable, and scannable in under 30 seconds?"

🔄
Design Process
03
Process for Business Dashboard
Stakeholder Interviews
Understand business goals, data sources, and reporting pain points
Competitive Analysis
Benchmark against leading enterprise dashboards — Datadog, Mixpanel, Tableau
User Persona & Journey
Define primary persona — Business Analyst / Operations Manager
Information Architecture
Structure data hierarchy — Overview → Drill-down → Action
User Flow Mapping
Map end-to-end flows for core tasks: monitoring, reporting, alerting
Wireframes → Visual Design
Low-fidelity layout explorations, then high-fidelity UI — data-dense but clean, with clear visual hierarchy
🔭
Benchmarking Enterprise Dashboards
04
Benchmarking Enterprise Dashboards

Analysed competing dashboards to identify what works, what frustrates users, and what opportunities exist to differentiate.

📊 Tableau
High data density, highly customisable, but steep learning curve for new users
📈 Mixpanel
Medium data density, strong analytics focus, good learnability for product teams
🐶 Datadog
High data density, low customisability, optimised for engineering/ops power users
→
Most enterprise dashboards optimise for power users — the learning curve is steep and first-time operators struggle to extract value quickly
→
Alert fatigue is common — tools surface too many notifications without smart prioritisation, causing operators to ignore critical issues
→
Opportunity: Contextual defaults — show what matters most by role, with progressive disclosure for deeper analysis
👤
User Persona
05
Primary Persona — The Business Analyst

Priya Rajan — Senior Business Analyst · B2B SaaS · Bangalore · 31 · Power user, data-driven

Scenario: Priya monitors KPIs across 3 product lines every morning. She needs to quickly identify anomalies, drill into causes, and escalate issues before the 9am stand-up. She currently switches between 4 tools and copy-pastes data into a shared spreadsheet every day.

Goals
Single view of all product KPIs · Spot anomalies in under 60 seconds · Shareable reports in one click · Customise view by product / date
Pain Points
Too many tools, no single source of truth · Manual report compilation takes 45 min/day · Alert overload — hard to find critical issues · No drill-down without leaving dashboard
🏗️
Information Architecture
06
Structuring the Dashboard Hierarchy

The IA follows an Overview → Module → Detail pattern — allowing users to scan the full picture first, then progressively drill into specific areas.

🏠 Dashboard Home📊 Overview — KPIs · Trends · Alerts📦 Products — Per-product drill-down📋 Reports — Export · Schedule · Share⚙️ Settings — Alerts · Users · Integrations
🔀
User Flow
07
Core Flow — Monitor & Act on a KPI Alert
01 — Login → Dashboard Home
Priya sees the Overview screen with all KPI cards and trend sparklines at a glance
02 — Anomaly Alert Surfaces
A red badge on the Transactions KPI card — 18% drop overnight. Alert panel expands
03 — Click Alert → Drill-Down View
Full transaction module loads — time-series chart, failure breakdown by product line
04 — Apply Filters
Filter by date range, product, and geography to isolate the failing segment
05 — Identify Root Cause
Payment gateway failures spike in one region — visible in the geographic heatmap widget
06 — Escalate / Export
One-click export to PDF or share filtered view URL with the engineering team
🚀
Design Outcomes
08
Impact & Results
Unified View
Consolidated 4 separate reporting tools into a single dashboard — eliminating manual copy-paste and reducing daily reporting time from 45 min to under 5 min.
Smart Alerting
Anomaly detection surfaced on the primary view — critical issues now identified in under 30 seconds vs previously going unnoticed until stand-up.
Scalable System
Modular IA allows new product data to be plugged in without redesign — the dashboard scales horizontally as the product portfolio grows.
Stakeholder Adoption
Progressive disclosure design reduced cognitive load — even non-technical stakeholders could read KPIs and drill down without training.

!

Define — User Persona
04
Meet Sunilkumar

Sunilkumar — Senior Lead, Software Company · Bangalore, India · 33 · Married, 2 kids

Scenario: Sunil loves long road trips with his family. He travels Bangalore–Hyderabad once a month. He tracks all travel expenses for tax-exemption reports, and prefers digital payments.

Goals

Ideate — UX Strategy & Principles
05
Design Principles Applied
→
Reward users for joining — Referral bonus to build network effect
→
Let users see value quickly — Pre-login features: rate calculator, toll estimator, branch locator

Reduce cognitive load — Intuitive UI that minimises visual, intellectual, memory and motor load

Project UX Revamp
03
Project UX Revamp — Why revamping?

A UI that is not clear, not easy to understand, confusing, boring tends to spoil the experience of (prospective) customers. People want to experience good applications.

Quick Findings
Unified experience — good in a way. Standards are poor though — Plain, old, dated look.

PRDs lack clear goals · Unclear redesign goals · Single person perspective · No deep thoughts for customization
Shortcomings
Lack of holistic perspective · Lack of business context in the design team · Lack of knowledge about users (Needs, Goals, Pain points, Context of use, Competition)
Why restructuring is needed
→
Need to create strong leaders · Create a centralized design system — communication, strategy, knowledge building, direction, and processes that could hold the design practice together
→
Create a system that enables people to be aligned in the direction for growth · Businesses need to articulate their vision and set clear goals
📊
B2B UX Metrics & UX Maturity
04
B2B UX Metrics

With growing competitiveness in the B2B industry, B2B companies are also starting to value user experience. These B2B companies can leverage on quality user experience to stand out in a crowded market. A good UX design helps bridge the gaps in the process, making it more friendly for the users.

Due to differences in business characteristics, it is difficult to directly apply the more mature B2C UX metrics to B2B products. It is crucial to pay equal attention to user behaviour and application performance.

PerformanceTask experienceEngagementClaritySatisfaction
UX Maturity

UX maturity measures an organization's desire and ability to successfully deliver user-centered design. It encompasses the quality and consistency of research and design processes, resources, tools, and operations, as well as the organization's propensity to support and strengthen UX now and in the future, through its leadership, workforce, and culture.

⚖️
Product UX Principles
05
Product UX Principles

"A good software program or website should let people accomplish their intended tasks as easily and directly as possible." — Steve Krug, author of 'Don't Make Me Think'

Don't make me think
A good software program lets people accomplish their intended tasks as easily and directly as possible
There is power in suggestion
Never seek to persuade anyone of something you yourself would not want to be persuaded. Use persuasion only for the good of user.
Being ethical is important
Deception is never ethically justifiable. Try to keep from dark patterns. Avoid sneaky designs and confusing language.
Leverage UX as a strategic differentiator

Design exceptional digital experiences to deliver value to businesses. We believe in design's ability to simplify, amplify and delight. Integrate design into culture and long term product strategy.

Research Case Study
Name Hunting · Product Naming Research
🔤 Pay@Ease · Product Naming Research
Name Hunting Research

To understand how Pay@Ease resonates with common people, and to find a product name that users can intuitively connect with BNPL.

238
Users Researched
14
Locations
216hrs
Field Research
Qual + Quant
Methods
🔍
Research Goals
01
Research Goals
→
To validate how Pay@ease resonates with common people as a service
→
To identify similar players and their positioning of BNPL service in the market
→
To understand the common people's perception of integrated BNPL as a service
→
To understand if people can connect the name "Pay@Ease" with a BNPL service
📊
Field Research
02
Field Research Findings

We conducted user research with common people to understand their preference for various modes of payment, context of use, idea of BNPL, and various BNPL services they are aware of. A team of 3 designers spoke with 15 potential participants from various backgrounds, each session 15–20 minutes.

!
13/15 participants had no idea what Pay@Ease means when they saw it first time
!
12/15 participants could immediately understand the terms 'Pay Later' and 'Buy Now Pay Later'
!
8/15 users learnt about BNPL from merchant sites like Swiggy, Zomato, Amazon, Flipkart
🏭
Name Hunting Workshop
03
Name Hunting Workshop

We held two workshops with 22 participants lasting about seven hours, to ensure that the product name is not biased. During the first round we selected 30 different names; in the second stage we narrowed those down to the 8 most suitable for the product.

Pay@LaterPay Later PlusEasy Pay LaterPay You LaterPay Me Later

We conducted Guerrilla Research with 238 users — 14 UXers & researchers, 07 teams, 216 hours field research, 14 locations (Metro stations, Shopping Malls, Coffee Shops, Beaches, Cinema Theaters).

🏆
Research Findings
04
What Worked Best
Easy Pay Later — 79/238
Gives a sense of Freedom · Feels positive · Easy to understand and remember · Creates Trust & comfort
Pay Me Later — 79/238
Friendly and personal · Communicates meaning clearly · Easy to understand and remember · Common layman term
Pay@Later — 47/238
Unique · Techy · Short & Simple · Direct tone · The "@" symbol adds distinctiveness

Overall, 'Easy Pay Later' and 'Pay Me Later' were almost equally preferred — both chosen for being "easy to understand, easy to remember, creates trust." 90% of respondents were Non-BNPL users, and interestingly the order of preference did not change with this data.

Study 01
01
M2P Gift Card — Redemption Experience Research Report · Apr 2023

The goal of this research is to gain a deeper understanding of the factors that inform the way users try to claim their rewards / gift coupons. This research specifically focuses on "overall redemption experience", how users perceive or rate the product experience. The final goal is to recommend or create an optimised flow for redemption with utmost ease.

The study utilized a qualitative approach to gain in-depth insights into users' experiences and perceptions related to the redemption process.

Key Findings
→
Lack of Context: On the landing page there is no reference to 'M2P' anywhere. 10/12 users were not aware of the brand 'LivQuik' on the landing page, and this made them feel they had clicked on a phishing link.
→
Lack of Support: All users found it very difficult to type the User ID again and again. 12/12 users faced challenges in remembering their autogenerated User ID.
→
Lack of Clarity: 12/12 users were not able to find what was the rewarded Gift amount. 12/12 users expected to see the details of the gift upfront.
→
Positives: All 12 users were happy to receive a personalised message with their name — a clear indication that personalisation is highly valued.

"Thought it would be a fraudulent/Phishing SMS. I will not open it!" — User quote during research

🔍
Study 02
02
Fleet-Customer Portal — UX Review

Purpose of portal: To streamline fleet operations, which ultimately helps customers/businesses improve their operational efficiency. Customers can manage Fastag, Fuel, and all sorts of vehicle expenses through this portal.

Business Objectives
Increased sales · Decreased customer support costs · Customer stickiness - increased retention · Increased customer acquisition · Decreased training costs
Positives Found
Customer/Business can manage all FasTag, fuel, and vehicle related expenses in one place. Seamless payment gateway. 2FA security boosts customer trust.
Review Findings — Shortcomings
→
Portal completely outdated
→
No proper hierarchy — difficult to locate features
→
The information architecture does not match with the mental model of users
→
No consistency in design — users will be confused, frustrated and will feel dislocated
→
To recharge the wallet, users unnecessarily have to go through 7 clicks
UX Plan
Improved IA & NavigationEfficient Search / Filter / SortSimplified User FlowsApply Design System
💳
Study 03
03
M2P Logo on Cards — Research Report

Business Goal: "To gain more visibility in the market as a brand." Branding is not just a benefit for the present but an investment for M2P's future.

21
Total Banks
152
Total NBFCs
86%
NBFCs with M2P Brand
Key Research Findings
→
Banks: Most banks (57.5%) have M2P logo on their cards. Banks who are aware of network standards REFUSE to have the M2P logo on debit or credit cards.
→
NBFCs: 86% of NBFCs have M2P branding on their cards. Big NBFCs like Jupiter, UNI, Slice do not have M2P branding.
→
Key Observation: BD does not insist much with some clients on having M2P identity on cards, since they are afraid clients might move to other providers.

"We are partnering with M2P only for TSP, hence we are not considering to add M2P's logo on our cards." — IDFC, Razorpay, Jupiter Edge

Recommendation

To the newly onboarding banks/NBFCs, M2P may consider including M2P brand as a little text on the back of the cards (e.g., "Powered by M2P"). M2P needs to create a strategic plan to take this forward in a highly diplomatic manner.

🔤
Study 04
04
Pay@Ease — Product Naming Research & Name Hunting Workshop

Pay@Ease is a plug & Play payment option that can be integrated with any payment gateway providers or a standalone Buy Now Pay Later solution. The research goal was to understand how Pay@Ease resonates with common people and to find a name that connects to BNPL.

13/15 participants had no idea what Pay@Ease means when they saw it first time. From end-user perspective, any name that includes the terms 'Pay' and 'Later' will be inherently easier for users to understand BNPL.

Name Hunting Workshop

We held two workshops with 22 participants lasting about seven hours. During the first round we selected 30 different names; in the second stage we narrowed those down to the 8 most suitable. We then conducted Guerrilla Research with 238 users across 14 locations.

238
Users Researched
14
Locations
216hrs
Field Research
Easy Pay Later — 79/238
Gives a sense of Freedom · Feels positive · Easy to understand and remember · Creates Trust & comfort
Pay Me Later — 79/238
Friendly and personal · Communicates 'Buying Now and Paying Later' clearly · Common layman term
Pay@Later — 47/238
Unique · Techy · Short & Simple · Direct tone · The "@" symbol adds distinctiveness

Overall, 'Easy Pay Later' and 'Pay Me Later' were almost equally preferred with 39% and 38% respectively — both preferred for being "easy to understand, easy to remember, creates trust."
